title: Parts of an Expression
_notes: Source of truth for the 0.3 practice set. Typed answers (kind "num") carry "derive": terms · constant · coef:<term> · factors:<term>, so the answer is computed from q, never typed; every wrong value names its mistake "m" (one, pieces, tokens, flat, variable-terms, distinct-vars, drop-sign, hidden-zero, constant, coef-of:<term>, sum-numbers) and the build recomputes it. "multi" uses check term-of:<expr> · terms:<n> · coefficient:<n>; "match" uses check "coefficient". Chips: TERM blue, FACTOR purple, COEF yellow, CONST green. See docs/exercises.md.

exercises.prompt: How many terms does this expression have?
exercises.read: How many terms does six x plus four have?
say: Terms are the pieces that are added or subtracted. The first term is six x.
After the plus sign comes the second term, four. Nothing else is added.

wrong.why: The plus sign separates two pieces, so there is more than one term.
wrong.say: counted the whole expression as one term

wrong.why: 6, x and 4 are numbers and letters, not pieces separated by + or −. 6x is a single term.
wrong.say: counted the six, the x and the four separately

wrong.why: The plus sign separates terms; it is not a term itself.
wrong.say: counted the plus sign as a term too

exercises.prompt: What is the coefficient of the x term?
exercises.read: What is the coefficient of the x term in nine x plus four?
say: First find the term with x. It is nine x, which means nine times x.
The number multiplied by the variable is the coefficient. It is nine. The four is a constant, not a coefficient.

wrong.why: 4 has no variable, so it is the constant term, not a coefficient.
wrong.say: used the constant term, four

wrong.why: The coefficient belongs to one term. Do not add the numbers of different terms.
wrong.say: added the nine and the four

wrong.why: The term is 9x, not just x. The 9 is the number multiplied by x.
wrong.say: looked at the x alone

exercises.read: What is the constant term of x squared plus five x plus eight?
say: The expression has three terms. Two of them, x squared and five x, have a variable.
The term with no variable is eight. That is the constant.

wrong.why: 5 is the coefficient of 5x. It goes with a variable, so it is not the constant.
wrong.say: picked the five, the coefficient of five x

wrong.why: 1 is the hidden coefficient of x². The constant has no variable at all.
wrong.say: picked the hidden one in front of x squared

wrong.why: The constant is one term. Adding the numbers of different terms gives a number that is not in the expression.
wrong.say: added every number you could see, and the hidden one

exercises.read: Which of these are terms of three x squared minus five x plus seven? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three of them are terms: three x squared, negative five x, and seven. Terms are the pieces separated by plus and minus signs, and each keeps its sign.

options.why: It is the first piece, before any plus or minus.
options.say: Three x squared. It is the first piece of the expression, so it is a term.

options.why: The minus sign belongs to the term after it.
options.say: Negative five x. The minus sign travels with the term after it, so this is a term.

options.why: This leaves out the minus sign. The term is −5x.
options.say: Five x. This leaves out the minus sign. The term is negative five x. Not a term of this expression.

options.why: It is the last piece, added at the end.
options.say: Seven. It is the last piece, added at the end. A term with no variable is still a term.

options.why: x² is only part of the term 3x². It is a factor, not a term.
options.say: x squared. This is only part of three x squared. It is a factor inside the first term, not a term by itself.

exercises.read: What is the coefficient of negative x in four x squared minus x plus seven?
say: The second term is negative x. The minus sign belongs to it.
There is no number written, but a variable alone has a coefficient of one, and the minus sign makes it negative one.

wrong.why: The minus sign belongs to the term, so the coefficient is −1, not 1.
wrong.say: dropped the minus sign

wrong.why: No number written does not mean zero. It means one.
wrong.say: thought no number means zero

wrong.why: 4 is the coefficient of 4x², the first term, not of −x.
wrong.say: used the four from the first term

exercises.read: How many terms are in three a plus two b minus five c plus one?
say: Break it at each plus and minus. Three a is the first term and two b is the second.
Then negative five c, with its sign, is the third term, and one is the fourth.

wrong.why: The constant 1 is a term too, even though it has no variable.
wrong.say: counted only the terms with a variable

wrong.why: Numbers and letters inside one term are factors, not separate terms.
wrong.say: counted every number and letter

wrong.why: The plus and minus signs separate terms; they are not terms themselves.
wrong.say: counted every number, letter and sign

exercises.prompt: What is the coefficient of m?
exercises.read: What is the coefficient of m in negative two m cubed plus m minus nine?
say: The term we want is m, the middle one.
No number is written in front of m, so its coefficient is one.

wrong.why: No number written does not mean zero. It means one.
wrong.say: thought no number means zero

wrong.why: −2 belongs to the term −2m³, not to the term m.
wrong.say: used the coefficient of the first term

wrong.why: −9 is the constant term. It has no variable, so it is not a coefficient.
wrong.say: used the constant, negative nine

exercises.prompt: How many terms does this expression have?
exercises.read: How many terms are in five times the quantity x plus two, minus three y?
say: The parentheses hold a group together, so five times the quantity x plus two is one term.
The second term is negative three y. Two terms in all.

wrong.why: The minus sign outside the parentheses separates 5(x + 2) from −3y.
wrong.say: counted everything as one term

wrong.why: The + inside the parentheses does not split the term 5(x + 2).
wrong.say: counted the terms inside the parentheses as well

wrong.why: Numbers and letters inside a term are factors, not terms.
wrong.say: counted every number and letter

exercises.prompt: How many factors are multiplied in this term?
exercises.read: How many factors are multiplied in the term six x squared y?
say: Factors are the things multiplied inside a term. Start by writing the term as a product: six times x squared times y.
Now x squared means x times x. So the factors are six, x, x and y. That is four.

wrong.why: x² means x · x, so it is two factors, not one.
wrong.say: counted x squared as one factor

wrong.why: The 6 is a factor too, and x appears twice.
wrong.say: counted only the letters x and y

wrong.why: A term is a product of several factors; this one has more than one.
wrong.say: counted the whole term as one factor

exercises.prompt: Select all the expressions with exactly three terms.
exercises.read: Which of these expressions have exactly three terms? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three expressions have exactly three terms. Count the pieces separated by plus and minus, and treat each group in parentheses as one piece.

options.say: Two x squared minus five x plus one. Three pieces separated by signs. Three terms.
A minus b plus c. The pieces are a, negative b and c. Three terms.

options.why: The group 4(x + 1) is one term, so there are only two terms.
options.say: Four times the quantity x plus one, minus seven. The group counts as one term, so there are only two terms.

options.why: Two terms: 3xy and 2. The x and the y are factors inside one term.
options.say: Three x y plus two. Two terms. The x and the y are factors, not separate terms.
Negative x plus six minus four y. The first term starts with a minus sign, but it is still one term. Three terms in all.

exercises.prompt: Select all the terms whose coefficient is −1.
exercises.read: Which of these terms have a coefficient of negative one? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three of them have a coefficient of negative one: negative x, negative y squared, and the negative group. A minus sign with no number means negative one.

options.why: No number is written, so the coefficient is 1, and the minus sign makes it −1.
options.say: Negative x. No number is written, so the coefficient is one, and the minus sign makes it negative one. Yes.

options.why: Its coefficient is +1: there is no minus sign.
options.say: x. The coefficient is positive one, because there is no minus sign. No.
Negative four x. The coefficient is negative four, not negative one. No.

options.why: Hidden coefficient 1 with a minus sign: −1.
options.say: Negative y squared. The coefficient is hidden. It is one, with the minus sign, negative one. Yes.

options.why: A minus sign in front of a group means −1 times the group.
options.say: Negative the quantity x plus two. The minus sign in front of the group means negative one times the group. The coefficient is negative one. Yes.

exercises.prompt: Match each term with its coefficient.
exercises.read: Match each term with its coefficient.
exercises.say_answer: Every term now has its coefficient. The sign belongs to the coefficient, a hidden coefficient is one, and an exponent is never the coefficient.

pairs.why: The number factor is 6, and the minus sign belongs to the term.
pairs.say: Negative six a. The number in front is six, and the minus sign belongs to the term. The coefficient is negative six.

pairs.why: No number is written, so the coefficient is 1.
pairs.say: b. No number is written, so the coefficient is one.

pairs.why: Hidden coefficient 1, made negative by the minus sign.
pairs.say: Negative c. The hidden coefficient is one, and the minus sign makes it negative one.

pairs.why: The exponent 3 is not the coefficient. The coefficient is the 9.
pairs.say: Nine y cubed. The exponent is not the coefficient. The coefficient is nine.

pairs.why: Hidden coefficient 1, made negative by the minus sign.
pairs.say: Negative d squared. The hidden coefficient is one, and the minus sign makes it negative one.

exercises.prompt: How many terms does this expression have?
exercises.read: How many terms are in two times the quantity three x minus one, minus x, plus nine?
say: The first term is two times the quantity three x minus one. The parentheses keep it together, so the minus sign inside does not split it.
Then negative x is the second term and nine is the third.

wrong.why: The minus inside the parentheses is part of the first term. It does not make a new term.
wrong.say: counted the terms inside the parentheses as well

wrong.why: The constant 9 is a term too.
wrong.say: counted only the terms with a variable

wrong.why: Numbers and letters inside a term are factors, not terms.
wrong.say: counted every number and letter

exercises.read: What is the constant term of negative x squared plus six x minus eight?
say: Two of the terms, negative x squared and six x, have a variable.
The term with no variable is negative eight. The sign goes with it.

wrong.why: The minus sign belongs to the term, so the constant is −8.
wrong.say: dropped the minus sign

wrong.why: 6 is the coefficient of 6x. It goes with a variable.
wrong.say: picked the six, the coefficient of six x

wrong.why: −1 is the hidden coefficient of −x². The constant has no variable.
wrong.say: picked the hidden negative one in front of x squared
